featured_reviews.name: Nisha Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
Long Post Alert!

Women's Hospital "Room Harmony" has been etched in my memory as it  was my home for two and a half months.
I had a complicated pregnancy and was advised completed bed rest and was admitted under Dr. Gayatri Rao's guidance who turned my hope into reality. She is the sweetest soul who would brighten my dark days with her encouraging words and smile.
On April 2nd, I delivered a premature baby boy after the long tiring journey.
I would also like to thank the nurses who had made my stay homely with utmost care and positivity. They were nice to me and somehow became my friends by the time I was leaving.
A big shoutout to sisters - Vidya, Hema, Trishala, Smita, Mayuri, Namrata, Alpa, Yashika, Sunita and I might have missed few other names but I am equally grateful to each.

Not only the nurses even the maushis were accomodating everytime I had to use the loo as I was on complete bed rest.

Last but not the least, I would also love to mention few other doctors who helped me with the littlest difficulty, doubt, concern even during the middle of the night namely Dr. Dipali, Dr. Vijaya, Dr. Shalini, Dr. Surti and Dr. Dolly.

Dr. Dipali was very empathetic soul who would keep visiting my room and appreciating and encouraging me to overcome each day in the hospital. Dr. Vijaya would flawlessly put the IV drip's on me with most care and concern avoiding any chances of hurting me. Also, Dr. Manju sinha would keep visiting and advising me to read books for a positivity.

Another appreciation I would want to give the phlebotomist who would come for my blood tests and would tell me lovingly that I would be a good mom. I forgot her name but I hope you guys will find out who she is.

It was a tumultuous journey for both me and my husband, but the way Dr. Gayatri Rao made my pregnancy possible with her positive smile and golden words is beyond everything.

It was a long stay but it became bearable with each and every person mentioned above. Thank you guys, for helping me out during the most fragile yet memorable time of my life. I will always be indebted to this hospital.

The only drawback if I may mention are the charges of the hospital as it is located at the posh side of bandra khar. But, for middle class people like us the charges were indeed challenging.

World Maternal Health Day: Every Mother Deserves Safe Care
Maternal health is not just a medical issue — it is a fundamental human right. Yet across India, thousands of women still face preventable complications during pregnancy and childbirth due to lack of access to timely, quality antenatal and obstetric care.

At Dr. Pallavi Shah's clinic in Andheri, maternal health is at the heart of everything we do. As a practising Obstetrician and Gynaecologist, Dr. Shah is committed to ensuring that every woman — regardless of the complexity of her pregnancy — receives respectful, evidence-based, and compassionate care.

Key maternal health facts every woman should know:

Pre-eclampsia affects 5–8% of pregnancies and is a leading cause of maternal and infant mortality if not identified early. Regular blood pressure monitoring at every antenatal visit is essential.

Gestational diabetes affects approximately 10–14% of pregnancies in India. Early screening and lifestyle management significantly reduce risks to both mother and baby.

Anaemia during pregnancy is alarmingly common in India, with iron deficiency affecting over 50% of pregnant women. It increases the risk of preterm birth, low birth weight, and maternal fatigue and complications.

Preterm labour (before 37 weeks) affects 1 in 10 pregnancies. Knowing the warning signs — including regular contractions, lower back pain, pelvic pressure, or unusual discharge — and seeking immediate care is critical.

Breast Health Awareness: Know Your Body, Protect Your Future
Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women in India, accounting for approximately 14% of all female cancer diagnoses. While these statistics are sobering, the message behind them is hopeful: when detected early, breast cancer has an excellent prognosis, with survival rates exceeding 90% at Stage 1.

The challenge is that early breast cancer often presents with no symptoms at all — which is precisely why awareness, self-examination, and routine screening are so critical.

Breast self-examination (BSE): Every woman above the age of 20 should perform a monthly breast self-check, ideally a week after her period ends. Familiarity with your own breast tissue helps you detect changes early.

What to look for:
• A new lump or thickening in the breast or armpit
• Changes in the size, shape, or contour of the breast
• Skin dimpling, puckering, or redness
• Nipple inversion (turning inward) or unusual nipple discharge
• Persistent breast pain not related to your menstrual cycle

Clinical breast examination: All women should have a clinical breast examination by their gynaecologist annually from age 25 or 30.

Mammography: Recommended annually or biennially from age 40 — or earlier for women with a family history of breast cancer.

Women with a family history of breast or ovarian cancer may benefit from genetic counselling and BRCA1/BRCA2 testing.

Contraception: Choosing the Right Option for Your Life Stage
Family planning is one of the most empowering aspects of women's healthcare—yet many women continue to rely on methods that may not be the best fit for their health, lifestyle, or future plans. With a wide range of safe, effective contraceptive options now available, every woman deserves a personalised conversation about what is right for her.

Common contraceptive options and who they suit:

Combined Oral Contraceptive Pill (COCP): Highly effective, regulates periods, reduces cramps and acne. Suitable for most healthy women. Requires daily consistency. Not recommended for those with certain clotting disorders or migraines.

Progestogen-Only Pill (Mini Pill): Suitable for breastfeeding mothers, women who cannot take oestrogen, or those over 35 who smoke.

Intrauterine Device (IUD / Copper Coil): Non-hormonal, long-acting (up to 10 years), highly effective. Good for women seeking hormone-free contraception.

Hormonal IUS (Mirena): Reduces or eliminates periods, excellent for women with heavy or painful periods. Effective for 5 years.

Injectable Contraception (DMPA): Once every 3 months. Suitable for women who prefer not to think about daily or weekly methods.

Implant (Nexplanon): A small rod placed under the skin of the upper arm — effective for 3 years with over 99% efficacy.

Emergency Contraception: Available for use within 72–120 hours of unprotected intercourse. Not intended for regular use.

Understanding Fibroids: What Every Woman Should Know
Uterine fibroids are non-cancerous growths of the uterus that appear during the reproductive years. They are extraordinarily common — studies suggest up to 70–80% of women will develop fibroids by age 50 — yet many women know very little about them until symptoms become severe.

Fibroids vary widely in size (from a pea to the size of a melon), number, and location within or on the uterus. Their location largely determines whether they cause symptoms.

Types of uterine fibroids:
• Submucosal — grow inside the uterine cavity; most likely to cause heavy bleeding and fertility issues
• Intramural — grow within the uterine wall; most common type
• Subserosal — grow on the outer surface of the uterus; may press on surrounding organs
• Pedunculated — attached to the uterus by a stalk; can twist and cause acute pain

Common symptoms include heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding, pelvic pressure or pain, frequent urination, constipation, backache, and in some cases, difficulty conceiving or complications during pregnancy.

Importantly, many fibroids cause no symptoms at all and are discovered incidentally during routine ultrasound.

Let’s separate myths from facts.

What Exactly is Ultrasound?

Ultrasound uses sound waves to create images of the inside of your body.

👉 It does NOT use radiation (unlike X-rays or CT scans).

❌ False

Ultrasound has been used for decades worldwide and is considered safe when performed appropriately.

It does not expose the mother or baby to harmful radiation.

❌ Not true when medically advised

Ultrasounds are done based on medical need.For example:





Early pregnancy confirmation



Growth monitoring



Detecting complications

👉 When recommended by a doctor, they are safe and important.

Ultrasound is:

✔ Non-invasive✔ Painless✔ Takes only a few minutes

Some mild pressure may be felt, but there is no discomfort.

Your doctor may advise an ultrasound if you have:





Missed or irregular periods



Pregnancy confirmation

Routine pregnancy monitoring

featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this with immense gratitude and respect in my heart for Dr Aparna ma'am who came like a blessing in my life when I was at my lowest. I was completely hopeless and even had negative self harming thoughts at times because of the medical trauma due to my prolonged illness. I have been dealing with recurrent UTIs since my early puberty and had incontinence issues since childhood too. I used to get sudden urge to go to the toilet which lead to me developing a bad habit of holding pee. Later during my puberty I got back to back UTIs and burning sensations. I also had constipation since this time. In 2014 (15 yrs old) I first time went to doctor with complain of burning sensation and got diagnosed with UTI. The doctor prescribed me medicines including antibiotics and gels. As I grew up the issue didn't seem to resolve despite visiting multiple doctors and getting many treatments. By 2018 I started having extreme pain around my whole pelvic area that includes my bladder and urethra and was given multiple oral antibiotics and even prescribed Intravenous antibiotics for 2 weeks after oral medicine stopped affecting fot my infections. By this time I had already visited multiple doctors but in 2019-2020, Covid 19 outbreak happened and I could not continue my treatments and I suffered immense pain. Later in 2021 I went to SGPGI, Lucknow where multiple check ups and treatments were given. I was referred to the Anesthesia dept for pain management since the urology meds were not helping with the pain. I had to go through excruciating pain which lasted for 15 hours a day and this happened on a daily basis.I was also given 2 nerve blocks (in 2021 - 2022) to stop the pain, both of which did not work unfortunately. I also developed a gynecological issue and noticed a lump near my urethra which was a cyst like protrusion from the mucosa lining. I got checked by a Gynecologist who could not diagnose its root cause. However, in 2024, I got admitted twice again in Sgpgi where my cystoscopy was done and only inflammation was reported in my bladder referring to severe cystitis.

When I met her for the first time she talked to me with motherly care and assured me that I will be cured. She was were very patient and attentive and made sure that I get comfortable to tell her about the symptoms thoroughly and gave a lot of time and attention to each and every single detail. I could open up before her freely because of her caring and kind nature. After going through all my reports from previous 14 years of treatments she did several test and one of which was the sonography at Cama where she is an Assistant Professor and works pro bono. After all the tests my proper diagnosis was done and it was severe cystitis as well as the lump. She suggested several treatments including surgery, cystoscopy, hydrodistension as well as bladder instillations. She has also helped me financially and upon my request she did my surgery for cyst and a cystoscopy with hydrodistension at Cama Hospital. I was under a lot stress about the finances and the co-operation and understanding from my doctor but she made it seemless for me and I am actually in amaze how everything has turned out after so many years of hopelessness. I am recovering better now with the help of medications and instillations as adviced by her.

I truly dont believe any amount of words would be enough to express my gratitude to Dr Aparna Ma'am and her staff who were very very co-operating and kind and made me comfortable throughout the tests and appointments. I received her help in a way I could not have imagined. She is an amazing doctor and is very passionate about her work and a great philanthropist too. I admire her deep sense of service and the way she addresses and assures her patients. The way she counsel her patients is itself so helpful that brings out faith and hope to fight and overcome the illness and I wish her and Doctors like her always be blessed. A true gift to mankind. :)

If you are looking for a doctor who will hold space for the birth you hope for — rather than the one that's most convenient — Dr. Manjiri is who you want in that room.
